newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: U.S. Marines land in Freetown to evacuate Americans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines land in Freetown to evacuate Americans.

text.p: U.S. helicopters from a warship landed Marines in Sierra Leone capital on Friday to evacuate Americans despite an order by coup leaders in the West African state to close the country's airspace, witnesses said.
Four helicopters from the warship Kearsarge landed Marines with military vehicles at a hotel in Freetown were Americans were assembling to be evacuated.
The Marines quickly deployed and secured the perimeter of the hotel supplementing a Nigerian military force already there.

There was no sign of the Sierra Leone armed forces whose new military leader closed the country's airspace and banned domestic and international flights on the eve of the start of the U.S. evacuation.
The United States had said it would go ahead with the planned evacuation of about 250 American citizens from Freetown on Friday because of the unstable situation in Sierra Leone.

A U.S. Embassy statement, issued before the state radio announcement, told Americans who wanted to leave to assemble at a city hotel early on Friday to be transported by helicopter to the Kearsarge. They would then be taken to Conakry, Guinea.
